long_biography.plain_text:
At 18, Andy Scott used an inheritance from his grandmother to buy and renovate a Portsmouth house, doubling the money on sale. He combined building work with nightclub security and guest-house operations, then traded into larger hotels and housing projects. By his mid-twenties he had made his first million from property.

The 2008 financial crisis wiped out much of that business and left him with six years of recovery. Scott returned to building sites before establishing REL Capital as a turnaround investor. Its model takes controlling stakes in struggling small companies while existing managers retain ownership and operating responsibility. In 2025, he began selling most UK operating interests to concentrate on investment activity in the United States.

Andy Scott is an entrepreneur and Housebuilder from the UK.

He started his career working on the door of large nightclubs aged 16. Having always possessed an entrepreneurial spirit he soon began looking at other ways to earn a living and purchased his first property two years later with £5,000 left to him by his grandmother. He made his first million aged 26 from property and has since developed a multi-million-pound portfolio of over 500 homes across the UK through his various property development companies.

His journey was not always straight forward, having lost £6 million to the credit crunch in 2008 and breaking both legs in a car accident shortly after. However, by going back to his roots and returning to the building sites, Andy was able to successfully rebuild his businesses. The prolific deal maker has since expanded his focus to develop hotel nightclub and bar chains, including 1 Leicester Square, the West End’s biggest venue.

A specialist maritime profile also identifies this Scott with a different, historically owned vessel, but no public source reviewed names the owner of the upstream current vessel. Vessel evidence is not used in biographies, classifications or tags.

The dossier does not infer wealth from the label entrepreneur. Scott's first-person account and independent profiles trace inherited cash into a specific house purchase, renovation and profitable sale, followed by hundreds of property developments and millionaire status. Companies House later documents direct economic rights in a REL entity, while The Independent documents personal ownership of the SME portfolio. Exact current net worth and a complete asset schedule are not required or claimed.

It was not an inherited core business, operating asset or independently material share of the eventual fortune. Scott's renovation work, repeated property development and later investment business were independently substantial, supporting Self-made — advantaged start. The dossier does not claim that he inherited the later property portfolio, REL Capital or a family business.

Finance & Investments and Investor are based on those positive present facts, not solely on his historical REL title. The full private portfolio and relative asset values remain unpublished, so the current-sector score is High rather than Very high.

Current classification instead rests on the active Florida REL Investment Management company, retained litigation-funding operations and direct 2026 acquisition activity. The official REL website remains useful for founder identity and current operating descriptions but is read alongside the newer register and disposal evidence.
